content.comment_body: Hello, I have a fairly large project built with function blocks. I accidentally pressed the 'CONVERT TO LAD' button. All the function blocks were changed to Ladder configuration; after toggling the option back, the 220 blocks I had neatly organized were scattered randomly across the workspace. Is there a way to restore the previous arrangement so my function blocks return to their original positions? It would be very difficult to manually realign everything. Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

When you convert an FBD diagram to Ladder, the original FBD diagram remains unchanged because the process creates a new diagram sheet. You still have the original FBD diagram unless it was deleted. If you deleted the original, unfortunately, you will need to reconstruct the previous arrangement manually.

Before reading your comment, I discovered that converting a diagram from FBD to Ladder actually creates a new copy instead of converting the existing one. Only the newly created copy is converted, which I missed due to having multiple diagrams open at once. Thanks for your help.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced confusion over how converting diagrams from FBD to Ladder works within the software. The main issue is that block alignment can seem disrupted after conversion, leading users to worry their original arrangement was altered. The discussion clarified that conversion makes a new diagram, keeping the original intact, but this detail can be overlooked when managing multiple open diagrams.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want the software to maintain, or easily recover, the layout and alignment of function blocks after accidental diagram conversion. They also expect clearer indications when new diagrams are created, to minimize confusion.
